title: John Lennon watches the Smothers Brothers perform in Los Angeles | 1974
content:
John Lennon and May Pang watched the Smothers Brothers perform at the Troubadour in Los Angeles, USA, on 12 March 1974.

There were two shows at the venue, at 9pm and 11pm, with tickets costing $3.50. Lennon and Pang were joined by Harry Nilsson for the second show. Also in attendance were Pam Grier, Linda Lovelace, Lily Tomlin, Leonard Nimoy, Helen Reddy, and Peter Lawford.

Lennon and Nilsson were drinking Brandy Alexanders, a mixture of cognac, crème de cacao, and cream. Prior to the show they sang an a capella version of Ann Peebles’ hit ‘I Can’t Stand The Rain’ to the rest of the audience.

Embed from Getty Images

Things got heated when a photographer attempted to capture some shots of Lennon’s table. Lennon shouted “F**k you!” at the snapper, which led to a heated discussion. Lennon said he had aimed the insult at a waitress, to which she responded, “Well, f**k you!”.

When Tommy and Dick Smothers took to the stage, Lennon and Nilsson persistently heckled them during their act. Tommy Smothers halted the show, telling the audience, “There’s a narrow line between bad taste and vulgarity, and you’ve managed to cross it.”

Separately, actor Peter Lawford approached the venue manager Chris Walsh, insisting that he take action to eject the hecklers. Walsh approached Lennon’s table, arriving shortly before the Smothers Brothers’ manager Ken Fritz. Lennon told Walsh, “I don’t have to shut up; I’m John Lennon!”

Fritz had even less success. After remonstrating with Lennon and urging Nilsson to keep his friend in check, Lennon landed a punch on Fritz’s jaw. A fight ensued and Lennon was thrown out by the club’s bouncers.

I went over and asked Harry to try to shut up Lennon. Harry said, ‘I’m trying – don’t blame me!’ When Lennon continued, I told him to keep quiet. He swung and hit me in the jaw. I hit him back and the first thing I heard was the breaking of glass.
Ken Fritz
Star-News, 14 March 1974
Embed from Getty Images

During the fracas Lennon’s glasses were knocked off and he was unable to see clearly. On Santa Monica Boulevard he fought with the venue’s doorman Kenny St John and two passers-by.

A photographer, Brenda May Perkins, attempted to take a picture of Lennon, but he swung at her, allegedly hitting her right eye. She filed a citizen’s arrest warrant against Lennon the following day, but it was dismissed on 27 March after deputy district attorney Robert Immerman interviewed Perkins and found “no visible sign of any trauma.”

The incident could well have resulted in Lennon’s deportation from the USA. He immediately launched a press campaign in an attempt to minimise the incident. He admitted being drunk but claimed not to have gone near Perkins.

It was my first night on Brandy Alexanders and my last (laughs). And I was with Harry Nilsson, who was no help at all (laughs).
John Lennon
Rolling Stone, 5 June 1975

The next day, Lennon sent a bouquet of chrysanthemums to the Smothers Brothers. An attached note read: “To Tom and Dick: Please accept these flowers as a gesture of peace. We humbly apologize for our bad manners. Love and tears, John and Harry.”

Another bouquet was sent to the Troubadour, and Lennon wrote letters of apology to Pam Grier and Academy Awards show producer Jack Haley Jr. The note to Grier read: “I apologize for being so rude and thank you for not hitting me. PS Harry Nilsson feels the same way.”
